claims.text: The as-cast NbTiAlZr refractory high-entropy alloy has a relatively uniform Zr distribution.
Increasing Zr concentration and annealing at approximately 1123 K will promote Zr segregation at grain boundaries in a NbTiAlZr-based alloy.
The proposed intervention will produce Zr-enriched serrated grain boundaries.
The Zr-enriched serrated boundaries will contain a stabilized interfacial phase.
Serrated grain boundaries distribute strain more evenly than straight grain boundaries.
Zr-induced grain-boundary serration will impede grain-boundary sliding.
Zr segregation will enhance grain-boundary cohesion at high temperature.
Serrated grain boundaries will delay creep failure.
Relative to a lower-segregation baseline, the modified alloy will have a significantly lower creep deformation rate.
Relative to the baseline, the modified alloy will have higher elevated-temperature specific yield strength.
Zr provides solid-solution strengthening that can contribute to elevated-temperature specific yield strength in a related Nb-Ti-Al-Zr-containing refractory high-entropy alloy.
The baseline alloy has standard Zr content and conventional annealing that produces minimal grain-boundary segregation.
The proposed improvements will hold from 1023 K to 1223 K.
Intergranular failure is a critical limitation for the proposed alloy over 1023–1223 K.
The magnitude of creep-rate and yield-strength improvement depends on Zr content and processing parameters.
Failure to observe grain-boundary segregation or serration, or failure to reduce creep rate beyond experimental error relative to the control, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention includes both higher Zr content and a distinct controlled annealing treatment, but the experiment also says processing is identical except for Zr modification. Elsewhere the control receives conventional processing, so it is unclear whether annealing is held constant or is a second changed variable.
